headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Replit Agent’s broad filesystem/network access can ingest Haystack outputs and act on them without strong verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack can call MCP servers and REST APIs, so its outputs may be routed into Replit Agent workflows. Replit Agent reads/writes Repl files and acts inside a persistent workspace, making file-based prompt injection plausible if Haystack writes untrusted content there. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than observed.
conditions: IF Haystack output is written into a Replit workspace file and Replit Agent parses it as instructions, injection is possible.
IF a shared MCP or file bridge is configured between the agents, attacker-controlled content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Add a strict content-delimiter wrapper around Haystack outputs.
Disable automatic instruction-following on imported files.
Require human review before Replit Agent acts on Haystack-generated text.
Use separate workspaces with no shared files.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all cross-agent content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and can call MCP servers, while Replit Agent handles secrets and deployment configuration in a writable Repl workspace. If sensitive code or secrets enter the shared workspace, either agent can move them over network boundaries. The pair lacks documented isolation between their data flows, so the safer reading is high risk.
conditions: IF secrets or deployment config are placed in the Repl workspace, Replit Agent can read them.
IF Haystack forwards workspace contents to external APIs or MCP endpoints, those contents can leave the environment.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared files; use environment injection only.
Restrict Haystack to non-sensitive corpora.
Rotate any secrets exposed in the Repl workspace.
Audit outbound destinations for both agents.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Replit Agent can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses in a persistent Repl workspace. Haystack can reach APIs and MCP servers, so if it is configured to operate on the same repo or workspace, both agents can mutate shared state concurrently. The profiles do not show locking or coordination, so conflict risk is high.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository or Repl workspace, concurrent writes can clobber each other.
IF Haystack uses MCP tools that mutate shared resources, git or filesystem state can diverge.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch or workspace.
Pause one agent while the other writes.
Use file locks for shared artifacts.
Require commits only from one designated agent.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack can generate retrieved answers or tool outputs, and Replit Agent can act inside a full-app builder workflow with shell and filesystem authority. If Replit Agent treats Haystack output as authoritative, errors can cascade into code changes, deployments, or commits. No verification step is documented between them, so the default pathway is dangerous.
conditions: IF Replit Agent consumes Haystack output without independent verification, incorrect facts can become code or deployment changes.
IF Haystack returns malformed or stale retrieval results, downstream actions can propagate the error.
mitigations: Require a verification step before any action.
Limit Haystack output to citations, not instructions.
Have Replit Agent diff and review proposed changes before applying them.
Block deployment actions until a human approves.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking against source documents.

E_compliance.rationale: Haystack is documented as touching anonymous usage statistics, while Replit Agent touches source code, secrets, and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl. That creates a compliance mismatch if regulated or sensitive data is introduced into the pair, especially because Replit Agent’s secrets handling and network egress are broader than Haystack’s documented data class. The other agent is cited because the risk is about their combined handling of data classes.
conditions: IF regulated data or customer secrets are placed into the Repl workspace, compliance obligations expand beyond anonymous statistics.
IF data retention or residency requirements apply to the shared workspace, the pair may violate them.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Document the data classes each agent may touch.
Review retention settings for the Repl workspace.
Restrict outbound transfers from both agents.
requires-engineering: map data flows to residency and retention controls.
